study.question: Can exposing both fields of each event to the nonlinear scorer improve the grouped-history incumbent, and does any gain require target queries?
study.hypothesis: Source-level observation: each current field score sees only its own field plus action/recency. Within the neither-match group, re-pairing category and brand across events with identical action and encoded recency/coarse-age cells leaves field marginals, original grouped features, context queries, and separate-field summaries invariant. This is a representation collision, not measured predictive harm. The incumbent diagnostic sample assigns 0.574 mean attention mass to neither-match events (0.911 of visible events), so lost within-event pairing could matter. Scoring a joint category+brand+common key before separate field readouts can break this collision without adding parameters. Whether these distinctions predict clicks, or require target conditioning, is unverified.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit ad-conditioned local relation scoring. DIN already scores behavior embeddings; joint event keys are a local adaptation, not a general novelty claim. Retain softmax/equal-group allocation and matched norms, unlike original DIN unnormalized intensity.

nearest_work.difference: Replace only scorer keys: own+common becomes category+brand+common for both field queries. Keep independent category and brand attention weights, values, equal group masses and output width.

Earlier joint read averages separate scalar scores and shares a consensus value weighting. Here sum event embeddings BEFORE nonlinear scoring, retain two queries and separate value weights, and use the later equal-group allocation. Thus this is not the prior consensus readout.

The primary source generates queries with cross-attention and stacks a field-sequence bridge. This proposal changes event keys only; it adopts no generated probes, packed views or bridge and claims no source reproduction.
Registry supplies only author README and a blocked publisher-paper record. No detailed DMR mechanism equivalence or novelty exclusion is asserted.

inherited_components: All frozen causal information, scoring, ownership and resource contracts
Complete paired_match representation and original classifier
Shared DIN-style d64-to64-to1 relation network, including query/key product
Separate field value readouts, equal occupied-match-group mass and parent norm matching
Optimizer, objective, dimensions, initialization order and training recipe
study.proposed_difference: Prospective 2x2: coupled_keys true/false crossed with target_query true/false. Coupled scores use a(q_c,c+b+common) and a(q_b,c+b+common); separate controls use a(q_c,c+common) and a(q_b,b+common). No extra trainable parameters, features or loss. Both retain independent per-field softmaxes inside the same match groups, and the same 16-vector readout. Diagnostics re-pair only brand within neither-match events with matching action, fine encoded recency and coarse histogram age, holding category/common/group marginals fixed. This intervention is diagnostic only, not a training input transformation.
predictions: Separate controls reproduce the incumbent and its matched context control at seed42 up to admitted numerical tolerance; failures prevent interpreting the new contrast.

The original feature block and separate summaries remain invariant under the constrained brand re-pairing; coupled summaries can change. Diagnostics must report eligible sample fraction and distinguish source capability from learned usage.
If joint keys help, coupled_target must beat separate_target and both frozen source bests on full validation AUC, with logloss and measured train/inference costs reported.

Target conditioning requires coupled_target versus coupled_context; report the difference-in-differences (coupled_target-separate_target)-(coupled_context-separate_context), not only the largest cell. A context gain alone supports event-key access without target specificity.
falsifiers: No coupled-target AUC improvement over paired_match and the incumbent leaves incremental utility unsupported. Equal or better coupled-context leaves a target-specific account unsupported.
If paired-key sensitivity is absent in trained diagnostics, learned use of the identified collision is unestablished even if AUC improves. AUC gain alone does not prove pairing is the useful signal.
Separate-control re-pairing changes above floating-point tolerance, or original features/group mass/padding/empty checks fail, invalidates the collision diagnostic or implementation.
If apparent gain disappears under paired seed43/44 comparisons or measured cost offsets quality gains, report preliminary/null utility and no efficiency advantage.
alternative_explanations: Joint keys change key norms, covariance, nonlinear activation regions, gradient coupling and field sharing. Identical parameter count does not control effective function class or optimization. A gain is initially a joint-key replacement effect, not pure category-brand pairing attribution.

Neither-group re-pairing is an artificial intervention. Label-free sensitivity does not demonstrate that naturally occurring pairs predict labels or that the diagnostic sample represents the population.
Coarse category/brand identities, hash collisions, redundant exact-match groups, temporal drift or seed42 selection noise could erase meaningful event-pair signals.

Earlier consensus reads, product/addition paths, group slots, normalization, density, entropy floors and centering were null or worse; those are distinct interventions and do not refute joint-key scoring.
Publisher static snapshot as-of dates remain unverified; this stays a benchmark result, not established production point-in-time validity.
